h1: Tamarind Garden Hotel Rayong — a city-centre garden hotel with spacious balcony rooms and value beyond its star rating
intro: If you're heading to Rayong and want a city-centre stay that isn't a narrow building tucked down a side soi — but a hotel with a garden, a pool, spacious rooms with balconies, and a price you can actually afford — Tamarind Garden Hotel is the name real reviews bring up most often in this bracket · It's a 4-star hotel in the Choeng Noen area, off Sukhumvit Road in central Rayong, open since 2013 and freshly renovated in 2024, which makes the rooms feel a lot newer · There are 90 rooms in total, each decorated differently, all with a private balcony, plus an outdoor pool with a kids' pool, a gym, and a leafy garden wrapped around the building · From around ฿1,100/night, scored 9.1 from 135 reviews on Trip.com, and 4.4/5 on TripAdvisor — ranked #8 of 64 hotels in Rayong city

body.html: Who Tamarind Garden Hotel is for, in a nutshell — at its simplest, Tamarind Garden Hotel is a place for people coming to Rayong for more reasons than just the beach · It isn't a beachfront resort that puts you to sleep to the sound of the waves, and it isn't a high-rise hotel inside a mall selling luxury · It's a 4-star city-centre hotel set in a leafy garden in the Choeng Noen area, off Sukhumvit Road, a location that makes getting in and out of Rayong easy while still keeping the beach a short drive away · It has been open since 2013 and went through a major renovation in 2024, so the rooms and common areas feel newer than the building's age would suggest · It's still very much open and performing well — TripAdvisor ranks it #8 of 64 hotels in Rayong city with a score of 4.4 out of 5, and it earns 9.1 from 135 reviews on Trip.com · Real reviews line up on who fits here: travellers in town for work or business, couples or families who want a city base and then drive out to the beach for the day, and anyone after good value without paying beachfront-resort prices · Another group that says they loved it are people who care more about a spacious room, cleanliness and the quiet of the garden than about nightlife or restaurants within walking distance · It plays the "good value" and "garden calm" cards well, at a price that's easy to reach

Location and getting around — Tamarind Garden Hotel sits on Soi Ruenkwan, just off Sukhumvit Road, in the Choeng Noen sub-district of Mueang Rayong · The location's strength is that it's central but not chaotic — the hotel is set back a little from the main road and surrounded by garden, so it's quieter than hotels right on the highway · For getting around, Rayong town, the malls and the shops are all a short drive away, while the nearest beach — Saeng Chan Beach is about a 15-minute drive — and if you're heading to Koh Samet you take a car to Ban Phe pier and then the boat, around 30–40 minutes in total · A big plus for anyone driving themselves is that the hotel has free parking and an EV charging point, very handy when you're using it as a base to drive around the province · One thing many reviews agree on is that there aren't many restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance — most are 200–400 metres or more away · So if you don't have your own car, plan to use a ride-hailing app or sort meals out in advance · Overall this location suits people with a car more than those who want to walk to everything

"I picked this place because I was in town for work and wanted easy parking — and got more than I bargained for: spacious room, leafy garden, mornings spent having coffee in the garden. It didn't feel like staying at a city-centre hotel at all."

Room types and decor — Tamarind Garden Hotel has 90 rooms in total, and what sets it apart is that each room is decorated differently, giving it more of a home feel than a hotel where every room on every floor is stamped from the same mould · It starts with the Superior Room at 32 sqm, which, even as the entry-level room, is bigger than the standard rooms at many Rayong hotels · Moving up, there's the Deluxe Room at 36 sqm and the Grand Deluxe Room at 40 sqm, which give you a lot of space for this price range · For families travelling in larger groups there's the Family Room with bunk beds, ranging from 32 to 64 sqm depending on the room type · Every room has a private balcony, a point reviews love because you can open it up to catch the breeze and look out over the garden · Inside, rooms have air-conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, a minibar with some free items, a safe, a work desk and free Wi-Fi · Many reviews rate cleanliness and sleep quality as high as 4.7 out of 5, and agree that the rooms are very clean, the beds comfortable, and bigger than the price suggests · Many rooms have a bathtub in the bathroom, a detail you don't often find at this price · After the 2024 renovation, reviews say the rooms look clearly newer and fresher — the paintwork, the furniture and the in-room amenities · For anyone working or taking online meetings, the work desk and the reliable Wi-Fi help too · If you want a particularly quiet room, ask for one facing the garden when you book

Facilities, pool and garden — the highlight that earns the hotel the word Garden in its name is the leafy garden wrapped around the building · The greenery around the hotel keeps the whole atmosphere quiet and relaxed, unlike the usual all-concrete city-centre hotel · In the middle there's an outdoor pool with a separate kids' pool, which puts families with young children more at ease and gives guests somewhere to cool off after a full day of driving around · There's a gym with equipment that works well, which several international reviews single out as more complete and cleaner than expected for a hotel this size · On top of that there's a bar, free private parking, an EV charging point, a banquet/meeting room, luggage storage and a 24-hour front desk · To be straight about it, the pool here is more for cooling off and relaxing than a long lap pool for serious swimming, and there's no full-service spa like at the big resorts · But in terms of garden atmosphere and quiet, it does well — and that's a distinctive charm that's hard to find in a city-centre hotel at this price

Food and bar — the hotel's main restaurant is Rice Mill, which serves mostly Thai food and is where the buffet breakfast is set out · Breakfast comes up a lot in reviews, with most praising how fresh it is, the variety of hot and cold options, and the good flavours — many say the breakfast is well above the room price · But to be fair, there are voices in the reviews saying the breakfast menu leans Asian and Thai, with limited Western options — anyone who mainly sticks to bread, bacon and Western-style eggs may feel the choice isn't huge · For other meals, since there aren't many places within walking distance, many people choose to eat at the hotel restaurant or drive out to find somewhere in town · There's also a bar for an evening drink in the garden setting · Overall, the food at Tamarind Garden does well on breakfast and is enough for the stay, but it isn't a hotel that pitches itself on fine dining or upscale restaurants — it's a fitting extra for the style of stay where you use the hotel as a base and head out

Service — service is another area that draws consistent praise in real reviews, and it may well be this hotel's biggest strength · Many of the staff are described as friendly, smiley and very helpful, especially the front-desk and housekeeping teams, who international reviews single out for their attentiveness and speed · The service score on TripAdvisor sits at around 4.5 out of 5, higher than the average for hotels in the same class · The 24-hour front desk helps with late check-ins, calling a car, and recommending sights and restaurants in town · But in fairness, some reviews raise a point about the safety of the electrical wiring in a few spots and would like the hotel to respond to complaints more quickly · Overall, service is still a strong area and one of the reasons many guests say they'd come back

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — pulled together from Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: very spacious and clean rooms, freshly renovated in 2024 so they look new, a balcony in every room, a leafy garden and quiet atmosphere, fresh and tasty breakfast, friendly and helpful staff, convenient free parking, and value that many rank among the top reasons to stay · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned point is the location with few restaurants and shops within walking distance — you need a car or a ride to make it convenient · Next is the breakfast leaning Asian with limited Western options, the hotel being away from the beach and coastal attractions so you have to drive out, and a few voices noting details of the building's systems · Most of these gripes are about setting the right expectations — if you know you're staying at a city-centre garden hotel that needs a car, not a beachfront resort within walking distance of restaurants, your satisfaction will be as high as the overall score reflects

"The room was clean and very spacious for the price, all the staff were lovely, and the breakfast was better than expected · The one downside is there aren't many places nearby to walk to for dinner in the evening, so you have to drive out a bit — but there's free parking, so it wasn't a problem for us."

Price and value — the starting price for a Superior Room is around ฿1,100–1,300/night in normal periods, rising to roughly ฿1,800–2,500 over long weekends or festivals · Bigger rooms like the Deluxe and Grand Deluxe run from around ฿1,500 up, while the Family Room with bunk beds still sits at a rate that's easy for families to reach · Compared with similar-class hotels in Rayong city, what Tamarind Garden gives you that many rivals don't fully match at the same price is surprisingly spacious rooms, a balcony in every room, a garden and pool, and a breakfast that earns praise · Once you add free parking, an EV charging point and attentive service, many reviews come to the same conclusion: it's one of the best-value hotels in Rayong city for people who don't need to stay right on the beach · If you're planning to use Rayong city as a base to drive around and you value a spacious room and quiet, every baht you spend feels like it comes back in full

Good to know before you book — a few things help make the stay smoother · One, if possible, have your own car or have a ride-hailing app ready, because there aren't many restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance · Two, if quiet matters to you, ask for a room facing the garden rather than one facing the road · Three, if you're set on a Western-style breakfast, be prepared for a menu that leans Thai and Asian, or plan to find a café/bakery in town · Four, make the most of the free parking and EV charging by planning to drive to Saeng Chan Beach, Ban Phe pier and the sights around town all in one day · Five, over long weekends and festivals rooms fill up fast and prices climb, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms, and choose a free-cancellation option if your plans aren't firm yet

The verdict — from everything the real reviews say, Tamarind Garden Hotel is the best fit for people who want a spacious, clean city-centre Rayong stay with a garden and pool at a genuinely good price · Rooms bigger than the price suggests, a balcony in every room, a 2024 renovation that makes everything look fresh, attentive service, and free parking with an EV charging point make it hard to find a rival at the same price in Rayong city · If you're after a resort where you can walk straight down to the beach, or want to stay in an area with restaurants and nightlife within walking distance, this may not be the answer — and you should consider somewhere near Saeng Chan Beach or on Koh Samet instead · But for a car-based trip where you want a quiet, good-value, well-run city-centre base, Tamarind Garden Hotel meets that brief almost completely — and it's why its real-review scores keep holding high

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Tamarind Garden Hotel Rayong

faq.q: Where is Tamarind Garden Hotel · is it easy to get to?
faq.a: The hotel is on Soi Ruenkwan, Sukhumvit Road, Choeng Noen sub-district, Mueang Rayong, central but set back into a garden so it's quiet · It's about a 15-minute drive to Saeng Chan Beach, and you can reach Ban Phe pier and take the boat to Koh Samet in around 30–40 minutes · There's free parking and an EV charging point · One thing to note is that there are few restaurants within walking distance, so it suits people with a car more

faq.q: What's the starting price at Tamarind Garden Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start around ฿1,100–1,300/night for a Superior Room of 32 sqm in normal periods · There's a Deluxe at 36 sqm, a Grand Deluxe at 40 sqm, and a Family Room with bunk beds for families · Every room has a private balcony · Prices rise over long weekends and festivals, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is Tamarind Garden Hotel for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers in town for work, couples, and families who want a spacious, clean, good-value city-centre base in Rayong and then drive out to the beach for the day · There's a garden, a pool, and free parking · If you're after a resort where you can walk straight down to the beach, somewhere near Saeng Chan Beach or on Koh Samet may suit you better

faq.q: Does Tamarind Garden Hotel have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes, there's an outdoor pool with a kids' pool in the middle of the garden, and a gym that reviews praise as complete and clean · Breakfast is a buffet at the Rice Mill restaurant that earns praise for freshness and flavour, but leans Thai and Asian, with limited Western options

faq.q: What are the rooms at Tamarind Garden Hotel like · were they really just renovated?
faq.a: The hotel has 90 rooms that are each decorated differently and were freshly renovated in 2024, so they look fresh · Every room has a balcony, air-conditioning, a flat-screen TV, a fridge, a minibar, a safe and free Wi-Fi, and many rooms have a bathtub · Reviews rate cleanliness and the sleep as high as around 4.7 out of 5 and say the rooms are bigger than the price suggests

faq.q: What's Tamarind Garden Hotel's review score · is it still open?
faq.a: It's still open as usual · It scores 9.1 from 135 reviews on Trip.com and 4.4 out of 5 on TripAdvisor, ranked #8 of 64 hotels in Rayong city · The most praised points are cleanliness, spacious rooms, attentive service, and value
